summary: Scan fields helps a farmer decide what to plant next. Instead of simulating crops with generic assumptions, it shows what actually happened on thousands of nearby 30-metre land spots, using NASA and USDA satellite-derived data. The farmer picks their area, last crop and goal (save water, protect soil, save money, or stay safe in dry years). The app shows the best next crops with plain-language reasons, whether the soil should rest or get a legume cover crop, a 12-month heat and water calendar, and how crowded each crop already is nearby, so that advice does not push everyone into the same crop. It is built for older farmers: large print, icons, English and Spanish, read-aloud, a printable card, and a shareable link so a relative can help.
details:
A large-print, two-language (English / Español) helper that tells a farmer what to plant next, whether the soil should rest or get a cover crop, and what the year looks like for heat and water. Every number comes from satellite-observed land near the farmer (NASA + USDA data through Google Earth Engine) or from a small, labelled rule of thumb. There is no machine learning in the advice.

Built for NASA Space Apps 2026, Field Shift.
